newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil surges in late trade, soymeal ends up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil surges in late trade, soymeal ends up.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures surged in late trade to close up more than half the daily trading limit on fund buying triggered by signals the market was oversold, traders said.
Soymeal struggled with bearish short-term technical indicators but closed higher in tandem with strong soyoil and soybean values.

Technical indicators showed soyoil was oversold and due for a correction, traders said. They pointed to the Bullish Concensus which fell to 13 percent as of Tuesday from 18 percent the previous week and 59 percent on May 5.
"It's all managed guys, funds, coming in here buying it," said Mark Cermak, trader with O'Connor and Co. "They started buying it right around 23.62 (cents per lb)."

Strength in soybeans also bolstered product markets, as did reports Brazil and Argentina were buying new crop U.S. supplies. Argentine traders said Argentina bought 60,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for October/November delivery and U.S. trade sources said Brazil bought 150,000 tonnes.
Soymeal ended $3.20 to $0.70 per ton higher with July up $3.20 at $280.30. Soyoil closed 0.70 to 0.61 cent per lb higher with July up 0.68 at 23.97.

On the day, Merrill Lynch sold 700 lots July soymeal and 100 August, Prudential Securities sold 400 July and 100 August and LIT and Griffin Trading each sold 300 July. Continental Grain bought at least 300 July and Cargill Inc bought 200 July, pit sources said.
In soyoil, Smith Barney and Iowa Grain each bought 200 July, Produce Grain bought 200 December and Cargill Inc bought 200 August and 100 July, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 29,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 32,072 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Tuesday's 14,958.
